chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who has a female slave and kisses her, is she permissible for his son? He said, 'With desire.' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'She is not prohibited (to the son) unless he kisses her with desire.' Then he began from himself, 'If he exposes her and looks at her with desire, she is prohibited to his father and his son.' I said, 'If he looks at her body?' He said, 'If he looks at her private part and her body with desire, she is prohibited to him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a master's son marrying his father's female slave if the father kissed her?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the prohibition of a concubine for the master and his son arises specifically from sexual desire (*shahwah*) during acts like kissing or gazing, rather than mere physical contact. This distinction highlights the juristic principle that the establishment of *mahramiyyah* (prohibition) through concubinage is contingent upon the intent and nature of the sexual act, a key topic in Shia fiqh regarding the rights of *Umm al-Walad*.
